Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: GPUMD 4.0: A high-performance molecular dynamics package for versatile materials simulations with machine-learned potentials

Mixed_Signals: Paper is a broad computational methodology/software review covering metals, ceramics, carbon materials, perovskites, etc. Routed as Metals based on prominent metal application examples (HEA 100M atoms, W radiation damage, 16-metals NEP model), but the software itself is material-agnostic.
Application is mixed: thermal transport (Functional), mechanical properties (Structural), electronic transport (Functional). Routed as Functional based on thermal/electronic transport dominance.
No additive manufacturing content despite group label suggesting AM; paper is purely about MD simulation methodology.

Raw_Evidence_Span: GPUMD 4.0: A high-performance molecular dynamics package for versatile materials simulations with machine-learned potentials
GPUMD incorporates native machine-learned potentials (NEP) and is optimized for GPU computing
the latest version of GPUMD, released in April 2025, is GPUMD 4.0
It contains about 85,000 lines of source code written in CUDA C++

Composition.Note: GPUMD 4.0 is a GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics simulation software package, not a physical material. It supports NEP, EAM, Tersoff, LJ, FCP, DP, ILP, and other interatomic potentials.

Process_Text.original: GPUMD is primarily developed using CUDA C++ (although it has also been adapted to work with HIP). Upon compilation, two executables are generated: gpumd and nep. The nep executable serves the training of NEP models, whereas the gpumd executable is designed for conducting MD simulations. For the nep executable, two files are required: train.xyz (training data) and nep.in (training hyperparameters). For the gpumd executable, at least two files must be provided: run.in (controls the MD simulation) and model.xyz (defines the system). GPUMD supports both conventional empirical potentials and machine-learned potentials including LJ, EAM, Tersoff, ILP, FCP, NEP, and DP.
Process_Text.simplified: GPUMD 4.0 is a CUDA C++ based GPU-accelerated MD package. Generates gpumd (simulation) and nep (NEP training) executables. Supports LJ, EAM, Tersoff, NEP, DP, FCP potentials. ~85,000 lines of CUDA C++ source code.

Simulation_Metadata.Ensemble: NVE, NVT (Berendsen, NHC, BDP, Langevin), NPT (Berendsen, SCR, MTTK), NPH (MTTK), PIMD, RPMD, TRPMD

Model_Size.Note: 100 million atoms simulated with 8x 80-GB A100 GPUs for high-entropy alloy (Song et al. [24])

Time_or_Step_Params.Note: Time step is user-configurable; no single default value specified

Simulation_Text.original: Using a single GPU, either professional or consumer grade, NEP-GPUMD can achieve a computational speed of the order of 10^7 atom-step per second in typical MD simulations. The number of atoms in the simulation cell manageable with a single GPU ranges from 1 to 10 million, depending on the device memory of the GPU. With eight 80-GB A100 GPUs, NEP has been used to simulate a high-entropy alloy with 100 million atoms.
Simulation_Text.simplified: NEP-GPUMD achieves ~10^7 atom-steps/s on a single GPU. Single GPU manages 1-10M atoms. 8x A100 GPUs used for 100M atom HEA simulation.

NEP_Computational_Speed_atom_step_per_s.Note: 原文: of the order of 10^7 atom-step per second (order of magnitude, not exact value)

Structure_Text.original: GPUMD is a software package, not a physical material. The NEP4 architecture uses a single hidden layer neural network with descriptor vectors consisting of radial and angular components. Radial descriptors use Chebyshev polynomial basis functions with trainable expansion coefficients. Angular descriptors use Legendre polynomials. The descriptor dimension is N_des, hidden layer dimension is N_neu. Activation function is tanh. NEP4 supports multi-element systems with element-pair-specific radial functions.
Structure_Text.simplified: NEP4 neural network architecture: single hidden layer, radial + angular descriptors, Chebyshev polynomial basis, Legendre polynomial angular descriptors, tanh activation.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Liang et al. [43] developed NEP89, a comprehensive foundation model covering virtually the entire periodic table
NEP89 achieves competitive accuracy compared to representative foundation models across a range of properties
while being three to four orders of magnitude more computationally efficient

Composition.Note: NEP89 is a comprehensive foundation model covering virtually the entire periodic table (89 elements). It can be used out-of-box or fine-tuned.

Process_Text.original: NEP89, a comprehensive foundation model covering virtually the entire periodic table, which has been released alongside GPUMD 4.0. NEP89 can be used out of the box or as a starting point that can be conveniently fine-tuned with a relatively small amount of additional training data for system-specific applications. NEP89 achieves competitive accuracy compared to representative foundation models across a range of properties, including energetics, elastic properties, phonon frequencies, and MD simulations of amorphous carbon, liquid water, and solid-state electrolytes, while being three to four orders of magnitude more computationally efficient.
Process_Text.simplified: NEP89 covers 89 elements (virtually entire periodic table). Released with GPUMD 4.0. Can be used out-of-box or fine-tuned. 3-4 orders of magnitude more efficient than other foundation models.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Song et al. [24] pioneered the development of large NEP models for multiple species
They successfully created a general-purpose NEP model for 16 metals and their arbitrary alloys
simulating 100 million atoms using only eight 80-GB A100 GPUs

Composition.Note: General-purpose NEP model for 16 elemental metals and their arbitrary alloys. Demonstrated substantially higher accuracy than conventional EAM.

Process_Text.original: Song et al. [24] pioneered the development of large NEP models for multiple species, emphasizing the importance of focusing on elemental and binary systems during data construction. They successfully created a general-purpose NEP model for 16 metals and their arbitrary alloys, demonstrating substantially higher accuracy compared to the conventional embedded atom method. This NEP model also achieved a computational milestone by simulating 100 million atoms using only eight 80-GB A100 GPUs.
Process_Text.simplified: Song et al. [24]: NEP model for 16 metals + arbitrary alloys. Higher accuracy than EAM. Milestone: 100M atoms on 8x A100 GPUs.

Model_Size.Note: 100 million atoms simulated for high-entropy alloy

Structure_Text.original: The NEP model for 16 metals demonstrated substantially higher accuracy compared to the conventional embedded atom method. Data construction focused on elemental and binary systems.
Structure_Text.simplified: 16-metals NEP model: higher accuracy than EAM, trained on elemental + binary data.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Yan et al.[233] initiated research on ion transport in solid-state electrolytes
NEP model to explore the effects of lithium nonstoichiometry on ionic conductivity and phase stability in Li7La3Zr2O12
ten-orders-of-magnitude increase in room-temperature ionic conductivity

Composition.Note: Solid-state electrolyte material. Studied lithium nonstoichiometry effects.

Process_Text.original: Yan et al.[233] initiated research on ion transport in solid-state electrolytes, a critical area for advancing all-solid-state battery technology. They developed a NEP model to explore the effects of lithium nonstoichiometry on ionic conductivity and phase stability in Li7La3Zr2O12. Their findings revealed that even minor deviations from stoichiometry, particularly lithium deficiency, significantly lower the activation energy for Li+ diffusion in tetragonal Li7La3Zr2O12. This leads to a remarkable ten-orders-of-magnitude increase in room-temperature ionic conductivity.
Process_Text.simplified: Yan et al. [233]: NEP for Li7La3Zr2O12. Li deficiency lowers activation energy for Li+ diffusion in tetragonal phase, causing 10 orders of magnitude increase in room-temperature ionic conductivity.

Structure_Text.original: Lithium deficiency in tetragonal Li7La3Zr2O12 significantly lowers activation energy for Li+ diffusion.
Structure_Text.simplified: Tetragonal LLZO with Li deficiency shows dramatically enhanced Li+ diffusion.

Properties.Test_Condition: Room temperature, tetragonal phase with Li deficiency
Properties.Note: 原文: ten-orders-of-magnitude increase in room-temperature ionic conductivity. This is a qualitative order-of-magnitude description, not a precise numerical value.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Shi et al. [152] initiated the study of shock compression using GPUMD and NEP
developed a NEP model for carbon at high pressures
discovery of the long-sought BC8 phase of carbon

Nominal_Composition.Note: Carbon model for high-pressure shock compression simulation

Process_Text.original: Shi et al. [152] initiated the study of shock compression using GPUMD and NEP. They developed a NEP model for carbon at high pressures, which demonstrated exceptional capabilities in modeling both the melting behavior and the Hugoniot line. They designed a thermodynamic pathway suitable for double shock compression experiments, facilitating the discovery of the long-sought BC8 phase of carbon.
Process_Text.simplified: Shi et al. [152]: NEP for high-pressure carbon shock compression. Discovered BC8 phase via double shock pathway.

Structure_Text.original: BC8 phase of carbon discovered through double shock compression simulations. The NEP model captured melting behavior and Hugoniot line accurately.
Structure_Text.simplified: BC8 carbon phase discovered via NEP-based shock simulation.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Ying et al. [166] were the first to apply GPUMD and NEP to investigate mechanical properties
study of a C60-based quasi-two-dimensional network
extended the scope to larger spatial and temporal scales, approaching strain rates that are almost experimentally attainable

Process_Text.original: Ying et al. [166] were the first to apply GPUMD and NEP to investigate mechanical properties in their study of a C60-based quasi-two-dimensional network. Their work demonstrated consistent results for quasi-static deformation processes when compared with quantum-mechanical calculations. Moreover, they extended the scope of their study to larger spatial and temporal scales, approaching strain rates that are almost experimentally attainable.
Process_Text.simplified: Ying et al. [166]: First mechanical properties study with GPUMD+NEP. C60 quasi-2D network. Consistent with quantum-mechanical results at near-experimental strain rates.

Structure_Text.original: C60-based quasi-two-dimensional network studied under quasi-static deformation.
Structure_Text.simplified: C60 quasi-2D network for mechanical properties.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Chen et al. [177] initiated the study of short-range order in GeSn alloys using GPUMD and NEP
uncovered intricate short-range order features that strongly impact the electronic band structure
coexistence of nanoscale short-range order domains

Process_Text.original: Chen et al. [177] initiated the study of short-range order in GeSn alloys using GPUMD and NEP. A compact yet representative dataset was constructed via farthest-point sampling to improve training efficiency and predictive accuracy. Through extensive statistical sampling, they uncovered intricate short-range order features that strongly impact the electronic band structure. Large-scale simulations revealed the coexistence of nanoscale short-range order domains, which is promising for optoelectronic applications.
Process_Text.simplified: Chen et al. [177]: NEP for GeSn SRO. Farthest-point sampling for dataset. Discovered nanoscale SRO domains affecting electronic band structure.

Structure_Text.original: Short-range order features in GeSn alloys strongly impact electronic band structure. Nanoscale SRO domains coexist in large-scale simulations.
Structure_Text.simplified: GeSn SRO domains affect band structure; promising for optoelectronics.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Wang et al. [299] have recently used GPUMD and NEP to study the melting transition in atomistically confined layered materials
noble gases and aluminum confined between two graphene sheets
tetragonal-packed configurations in the confined systems

Composition.Material_Name_Raw: Noble gases and Al confined between graphene sheets

Process_Text.original: Wang et al. [299] have recently used GPUMD and NEP to study the melting transition in atomistically confined layered materials. They developed NEP models for noble gases and aluminum confined between two graphene sheets at different pressures and temperatures. Although noble gases and aluminum typically form only close-packed structures, even under the extreme conditions of white dwarf stars, they discovered tetragonal-packed configurations in the confined systems. Upon heating, confined two-dimensional monolayers melt according to the two-step continuous Kosterlitz-Thouless-Halperin-Nelson-Young theory. However, multilayer solids transition continuously into an intermediate layered-hexatic phase before melting discontinuously into an isotropic liquid.
Process_Text.simplified: Wang et al. [299]: NEP for confined melting. Noble gases + Al between graphene sheets. Discovered tetragonal-packed configurations. Monolayer follows KTHNY theory; multilayer has layered-hexatic intermediate phase.

Structure_Text.original: Tetragonal-packed configurations discovered in confined noble gases and Al (normally close-packed). Monolayer melting follows KTHNY theory (two-step continuous). Multilayer: continuous transition to layered-hexatic phase then discontinuous melting to isotropic liquid.
Structure_Text.simplified: Confined systems show tetragonal packing (vs normal close-packed). Monolayer: KTHNY melting. Multilayer: hexatic intermediate phase.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Song et al. [65] were the first to apply NEP in conjunction with hybrid Monte Carlo and MD simulations
The Monte Carlo sampling with NEP is highly efficient
significant promise for investigating the effects of chemical order in multicomponent systems

Composition.Note: Referenced in Table 6: Zhao [245] (Ti-Al-Nb) and Song [24] (16 metals). Hybrid MC/MD applied to multicomponent systems.

Process_Text.original: Song et al. [65] were the first to apply NEP in conjunction with hybrid Monte Carlo and MD simulations. The Monte Carlo sampling with NEP is highly efficient, as it leverages the locality of the potential function. This approach holds significant promise for investigating the effects of chemical order in multicomponent systems.
Process_Text.simplified: Song et al. [65]: First hybrid MC+MD with NEP. Efficient MC sampling via potential locality. Chemical order in multicomponent systems.

Structure_Text.original: Hybrid MC/MD with NEP enables investigation of chemical order in multicomponent alloy systems.
